prompt: What are the best email marketing platforms for a small business?

trials.response:
For most small businesses in 2026, I’d narrow the field to these:

| Platform | Best for | Main strength | Main drawback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **MailerLite** | **Best overall for most small businesses** | Easy newsletters + automation + landing pages + forms | Less sophisticated CRM than HubSpot/ActiveCampaign |
| **Brevo** | Businesses wanting **email + SMS/WhatsApp** | Multichannel marketing and built-in sales tools | Some stronger automation/features require higher tiers |
| **Klaviyo** | **E-commerce / Shopify** | Excellent behavioral segmentation, flows and revenue tracking | Can get expensive as your contact list grows |
| **Kit** | Creators, bloggers, newsletters | Excellent subscriber tagging, sequences and creator monetization | Less suited to traditional local/service businesses |
| **ActiveCampaign** | Businesses needing **advanced automation** | Powerful workflow builder and segmentation | More complexity than beginners usually need |
| **HubSpot** | Businesses wanting marketing + **full CRM/sales stack** | CRM, sales and marketing in one ecosystem | Professional-level marketing gets expensive |

### My pick for a normal small business: **MailerLite**

It covers almost everything most small businesses actually need without becoming complicated:

**Newsletters → signup forms → landing pages → audience segmentation → automated email sequences → websites → analytics.**

Its current free tier includes up to **250 subscribers and 2,500 emails/month**, plus campaigns, three automations, a website, landing page and signup forms. Paid plans start around **$12/month**, with considerably higher automation/form/page limits. MailerLite

So something like:

**Facebook/Google/SEO → landing page → signup form → subscriber → welcome emails → sales offer → follow-up**

can all be handled inside MailerLite rather than stitching together five tools.

### Brevo is the stronger alternative if you want multiple channels

Brevo combines **email, SMS, WhatsApp, automation, forms, landing pages and sales tools**. Brevo+1

Its free plan allows **300 email sends/day**, and Starter currently begins around **$9/month**. Standard starts around **$18/month** and adds unlimited-contact marketing automation, a landing page, A/B testing and more advanced reporting. Brevo Help

For a business communicating heavily through WhatsApp/SMS, **Brevo can make more sense than MailerLite**.

### For an online store: **Klaviyo**

Klaviyo is particularly strong when customer behavior matters: purchases, abandoned carts, products viewed, customer value, segments, etc. Its free tier currently supports up to **250 active profiles and 500 emails/month**, including automations, segmentation and reporting. Klaviyo UK

For a Shopify/WooCommerce brand, I'd generally investigate Klaviyo before the more generic email platforms.

### For a newsletter/content business: **Kit**

Kit is built specifically around creators. Its free plan currently supports up to **10,000 subscribers** and includes unlimited landing pages, forms and broadcasts. The Creator plan adds unlimited visual automations and automated sequences. Kit

So for someone building a newsletter, YouTube audience, course, paid community or digital-product business, Kit is particularly compelling.

### When I'd choose ActiveCampaign or HubSpot

**ActiveCampaign** is worth moving to once your marketing starts looking like:

> Lead downloads A → visits pricing page → doesn't buy → gets workflow B → clicks product X → sales team gets notified → customer gets segmented differently.

Its current plans support increasingly sophisticated segmentation and marketing automation, with landing pages and CRM/e-commerce integrations on higher tiers. ActiveCampaign+1

**HubSpot** becomes attractive when the **CRM itself is central to the company**—sales reps, pipelines, deals, lead scoring, marketing and customer service. But it is a very different price category: HubSpot's current Marketing/Content Professional offering starts around **$900/month**, plus onboarding, so it's excessive for many early-stage small businesses. HubSpot

**Bottom line:** I'd start with **MailerLite** for a typical small business, **Brevo** for email + WhatsApp/SMS, **Klaviyo** for e-commerce, **Kit** for a creator/newsletter business, and **ActiveCampaign** when sophisticated automation becomes important.

For a small business in 2026, I’d narrow the field to **MailerLite, Brevo, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, Kit, and Zoho Campaigns**. The right choice mainly depends on whether you prioritize simplicity, automation, ecommerce, or cost.

| Platform | Best for | Main advantage | Main drawback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **MailerLite** | **Most small businesses / beginners** | Simple newsletters, automations, landing pages, signup forms and websites in one platform; paid plans include broad feature access. MailerLite | Less sophisticated CRM/automation than ActiveCampaign |
| **Brevo** | Businesses with lots of contacts | Pricing is heavily send-volume oriented; Free includes up to 100,000 stored contacts and 300 emails/day, while paid plans start around $9/month. Also supports SMS/WhatsApp. Brevo Help | Interface/marketing ecosystem isn't as polished as some competitors |
| **ActiveCampaign** | **Advanced automation** | Powerful segmentation, multi-step automations, ecommerce/CRM integrations and landing pages; plans start around $15/month. ActiveCampaign+1 | More complexity than a beginner usually needs |
| **Mailchimp** | Ecommerce + huge integration ecosystem | Mature platform with automation, AI features, audience analytics and extensive integrations. Standard currently starts around $20/month at entry levels. Mailchimp | Can become expensive as contacts and sending grow |
| **Kit** | Creators, newsletters, courses | Excellent tagging, sequences, landing pages and digital-product selling. Free plan supports up to **10,000 subscribers**; Creator is about $33/month for 1,000 subscribers when billed annually. Kit | Designed more for creators than traditional shops/service businesses |
| **Zoho Campaigns** | Budget-conscious businesses / Zoho users | Free plan supports **2,000 contacts and 6,000 emails/month**; paid tiers add unlimited emails, automation and deeper analytics. Zoho+1 | Best experience is within the Zoho ecosystem |
| **Constant Contact** | Local businesses wanting human support | Strong templates, social tools, signup forms and live support; paid plans currently start around $12/month before annual discounts. Constant Contact+1 | Automation/value generally isn't as compelling as MailerLite or ActiveCampaign |

### What I'd choose

For a typical small business that needs **newsletters + automation + landing pages + signup forms**, **MailerLite is probably the best starting point**. It gives you most of the important capabilities without making the product unnecessarily complicated. MailerLite

If your priority is:

-   **Cheapest + easy:** **MailerLite**
    
-   **Large contact database / SMS / WhatsApp:** **Brevo**
    
-   **Serious marketing automation:** **ActiveCampaign**
    
-   **Blog/newsletter/personal brand:** **Kit**
    
-   **Ecommerce + established integrations:** **Mailchimp**
    
-   **Already using Zoho CRM:** **Zoho Campaigns**
    

I would generally **not start with HubSpot purely for email marketing**. Its current Marketing + Content Professional package starts around **$900/month** plus a **$3,000 onboarding fee**, so it makes more sense when you need the broader HubSpot CRM/marketing stack. HubSpot

For a new small business with perhaps **0–5,000 subscribers, I'd start with MailerLite**, then move to ActiveCampaign only if your automation requirements become substantially more complex.

For a **small business**, I’d shortlist these platforms based on what you actually need rather than popularity alone:

| Platform | Best for | Main strengths | Main drawback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **MailerLite** | **Best overall for most small businesses** | Easy editor, newsletters, automation, landing pages, signup forms, websites | Less sophisticated CRM than heavier platforms |
| **Brevo** | Businesses wanting **email + SMS/WhatsApp + CRM** | Multichannel marketing, automation, large contact storage | Interface/features can feel more complex |
| **Mailchimp** | Businesses wanting a mature ecosystem | Templates, integrations, analytics, automation | Can become expensive as contacts grow |
| **Kit** | Creators, newsletters, courses, digital products | Excellent tagging, sequences, forms and landing pages | More creator-focused than traditional SMB-focused |
| **ActiveCampaign** | Businesses needing **advanced automation** | Powerful workflows, segmentation, CRM integrations | More complexity than many small businesses need |
| **Constant Contact** | Beginners wanting strong support | Easy editor, onboarding, live support, events/social tools | Advanced automation generally requires higher tiers |

### My pick for most small businesses: MailerLite

MailerLite currently bundles the things most small businesses actually need: **email campaigns, automations, landing pages, signup forms, segmentation, website tools and integrations**. Its free plan supports up to **250 subscribers / 2,500 monthly emails**, while the paid Comfort plan starts around **$12/month** and expands the automation, templates, forms and landing-page limits. MailerLite

If you want something more sales/CRM-oriented, **Brevo** is particularly interesting. Its free tier allows **300 emails/day**, and paid plans start around **$9/month**; the Standard tier starts around **$18/month** and adds unlimited-contact marketing automation, A/B testing, advanced reporting and a landing page. Brevo Help+1

**Mailchimp** remains a strong mainstream choice, particularly if you value its integrations and ecosystem. Its current Essentials and Standard tiers start around **$13 and $20/month**, respectively, while Standard provides substantially stronger automation and personalization. Its free tier is limited to 250 contacts. Mailchimp

**Kit** is the standout if your "small business" is primarily a **newsletter, personal brand, course or digital-product business**. Its free plan currently supports up to **10,000 subscribers** and includes unlimited broadcasts, landing pages and forms; advanced visual automations come with its Creator tier. Kit

**ActiveCampaign** is where I'd look once automation becomes central to the business—lead nurturing, behavioral segmentation, ecommerce journeys and multi-step workflows. Its current plans scale from limited Starter automations to unlimited automation actions on higher tiers. ActiveCampaign Help Center+1

So, in practical terms: **MailerLite for the typical small business; Brevo for multichannel/CRM; Kit for creators; ActiveCampaign for serious automation; Mailchimp for ecosystem/integrations; Constant Contact for hand-holding and support.**

If your requirement specifically is **“newsletters + automation + landing pages + signup forms in one easy platform,” MailerLite would be my first platform to evaluate**, with Brevo as the closest alternative.

For most small businesses, I’d narrow it to these:

| Platform | Best for | Why it stands out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **MailerLite** | Best all-around for small businesses | Easy editor, newsletters, automations, landing pages, signup forms, websites, and relatively simple pricing. MailerLite |
| **Brevo** | Best for large contact lists / budget-conscious businesses | Free plan allows up to 100,000 stored contacts and 300 emails/day; paid plans start around $9/month. Also supports SMS, WhatsApp and transactional email. Brevo Help |
| **Omnisend** | Best for ecommerce | Strong Shopify/ecommerce automations, product recommendations, abandoned-cart workflows, email + SMS. Free plan supports 250 contacts/500 emails monthly; Standard starts around $16/month before introductory discounts. Omnisend Help Center+1 |
| **Kit** | Best for creators/solopreneurs | Excellent tagging, automations, forms, landing pages and digital-product/newsletter tools. Particularly suited to bloggers, creators and course sellers. HubSpot Blog |
| **HubSpot** | Best if you also need a CRM | Email, forms, CRM, lead management and sales tools in one ecosystem. Great as a business grows, but advanced tiers become much more expensive. HubSpot+1 |

For a **normal small business starting from scratch**, I would start with **MailerLite**. It covers the things most businesses actually need—**newsletters + automation + landing pages + signup forms**—without forcing you into a complicated CRM ecosystem.

If you have an **online store**, I'd lean toward **Omnisend**. If you expect to maintain a **very large list but don't email everyone constantly**, Brevo's contact/send model can be attractive. If you're building a **newsletter, personal brand, course or creator business**, Kit makes more sense. And if email is just one part of a larger **sales/CRM system**, HubSpot becomes much more compelling. Brevo Help+1

So the simplest shortlist is **MailerLite → general small business; Omnisend → ecommerce; Kit → creator; Brevo → low-cost/high-contact-volume; HubSpot → CRM-heavy business.**

For a small business in 2026, these are the platforms I’d put on the shortlist:

| Platform | Best for | Why it stands out | Entry pricing\* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **MailerLite** | **Best overall for most small businesses** | Easy editor, newsletters, automations, landing pages, signup forms, website builder; good balance of simplicity and capability | Free up to 250 subscribers; Comfort from **$12/mo** MailerLite+1 |
| **Brevo** | Businesses wanting **email + CRM + SMS/WhatsApp** | Stores lots of contacts and charges largely around sending volume; transactional email and multichannel tools included | Free: 300 emails/day; Starter from **$9/mo**, Standard from **$18/mo** Brevo Help |
| **Klaviyo** | **E-commerce / Shopify stores** | Strong behavioral segmentation, abandoned-cart/product flows, revenue attribution and email/SMS automation | Free ≤250 active profiles / 500 emails; paid email plans start around **$60/mo** Klaviyo UK+1 |
| **ActiveCampaign** | **Advanced automation** | More sophisticated workflows, segmentation, conditional content, CRM/e-commerce integrations | Starts around **$15/mo** for <1,000 contacts ActiveCampaign+1 |
| **Mailchimp** | Businesses wanting a huge established ecosystem | Strong templates, forms, analytics, integrations and increasingly advanced automation | Essentials from about **$13/mo**, Standard about **$20/mo** at entry tiers Mailchimp+1 |
| **Kit** | **Creators, newsletters, courses and digital products** | Excellent tagging, sequences, creator funnels, landing pages and digital-product selling | Creator from **$39/mo** for up to 1,000 subscribers Kit Help Center |

\*Pricing changes with subscriber/contact count, sending volume, billing cycle and promotions.

### Which I would choose

**For a normal small business → MailerLite.** It covers the things most businesses actually need—newsletters, signup forms, landing pages and automation—without becoming overly complicated. Its current paid plans also bundle substantially more functionality as you move up. MailerLite

**For an online store → Klaviyo.** Its real advantage is using purchase and browsing data to trigger highly targeted ecommerce flows rather than merely sending newsletters. Klaviyo UK

**For sophisticated funnels → ActiveCampaign.** Choose it when automation logic and segmentation are more important than having the simplest interface. ActiveCampaign

**For email + SMS/WhatsApp/CRM → Brevo.** In particular, its free plan can hold up to 100,000 contacts while limiting sending to 300 emails/day, which makes its pricing model quite different from subscriber-based competitors. Brevo Help

**For a creator/newsletter business → Kit.** Forms, landing pages, broadcasts, sequences, tagging and visual automations are central to the product. Kit Help Center

If I were starting a **small business from zero today**, my first three to test would be **MailerLite, Brevo and ActiveCampaign**. MailerLite would be my default starting point unless ecommerce or unusually complex automation changes the requirements.
